newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Cyclone closes Australia's Griffin oil field.
newsitem.headline: Cyclone closes Australia's Griffin oil field.

text.p: Australia's offshore Griffin oil field was closed on Tuesday because of Tropical Cyclone Ophelia which is sweeping through the area, industry sources said on Wednesday.
The field, situated off western Australia, is operated by Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd.
The sources said the field and a floating storage vessel were disconnected to protect them from the cyclone.
A BHP spokesman later confirmed that the 80,000 barrels per day (bpd) field had been disconnected in order to move the floating production and storage vessels out of the path of the cyclone.
"Griffin was shut down on Tuesday to escape the cyclone," spokesman Ian McCoy told Reuter Australia.
McCoy said the field would remain disconnected until the cyclone had passed.
The industry sources said Griffin loading would face at least a five-day delay to allow time for reconnections and testing to make sure the field could operate smoothly once the storm has passed.
BHP has a 45 percent stake in Griffin. Other stakeholders are Mobil Exploration and Producing Pty Ltd, a unit of Mobil Corp of the U.S., with 35 percent and Inpex Alpha Ltd with 20 percent.
Industry sources said the operators of the nearby 90,000 bpd Cossack field were keeping a close watch on the cyclone in case they needed to disconnect Cossack vessels as well.

Cossack partners are BHP, British Petroleum Co Plc, Japan Australia LNG (MiMi) Pty Ltd, a partnership of Mitsui & Co Ltd and Mitsubishi Corp, Chevron Corp, Royal Dutch/Shell Group and operator Woodside Petroleum Ltd.
Weather Service Corp, an independent U.S. forecaster had warned earlier this week the cyclone would see top winds of 80 mph.
